lessons.title: Find the big idea
lessons.explanation: The main idea is the most important point a passage makes. Look for details that belong together.

workedExample.title: Notice the repeated purpose
workedExample.notice: Each detail tells what the neighbors did for the library.
workedExample.think: The details are not mainly about one person; they all support one shared project.
workedExample.prove: The final sentence names the result of the shared work.
workedExample.answer: The main idea is that neighbors worked together to improve their library.

activities.prompt: Collect the clues that point to one big idea.
activities.hint: Ask what the details have in common.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Library Helpers.

passage.text: On Saturday, Maya labeled the library's new shelves.
Mr. Ortiz repaired a loose table leg.
Three neighbors sorted donated books by topic.
By noon, the library was easier for everyone to use.

task.question: What is the main idea?

choices.text: Maya likes making labels.
Neighbors worked together to improve the library.
Libraries should only have new books.

evidenceOptions.text: On Saturday, Maya labeled the library's new shelves.
Three neighbors sorted donated books by topic.
By noon, the library was easier for everyone to use.

task.explanation: The separate jobs all led to a library that was easier for everyone to use.

correctFeedback.title: Big idea found
correctFeedback.message: You connected several details to the shared result.

lessons.title: Read between the lines
lessons.explanation: An inference is a sensible idea you build from details the author gives you.

workedExample.title: Use an action as a clue
workedExample.notice: Jon checks the weather and packs a raincoat.
workedExample.think: People usually pack a raincoat when they expect rain.
workedExample.prove: The forecast gives the reason for his choice.

activities.prompt: Choose the prediction that follows the clues.
activities.hint: Use what the character does and what the passage says.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Rainy Hike.

passage.text: Jon checked the dark clouds before leaving for the trail.
The forecast on his tablet showed a chance of rain.
He tucked a raincoat into his backpack.
His sister carried a map and a water bottle.

task.question: What can the reader infer about Jon?

choices.text: He expects that it may rain.
He plans to stay indoors all day.
He forgot to prepare for the hike.

evidenceOptions.text: The forecast on his tablet showed a chance of rain.
He tucked a raincoat into his backpack.
His sister carried a map and a water bottle.

task.explanation: The forecast and raincoat are clues that Jon expects rain.

correctFeedback.title: Clue-based prediction
correctFeedback.message: You used more than one detail to make a sensible inference.

lessons.title: Use context clues
lessons.explanation: Context clues are nearby words and actions that help you figure out an unfamiliar word.

workedExample.title: Look around the word
workedExample.notice: The sentence explains what the careful hands did.
workedExample.think: If a person gently moves a small object, they are handling it with care.
workedExample.answer: Delicate means easily harmed and needing careful handling.

activities.prompt: Use nearby clues to unlock the word's meaning.
activities.hint: Notice what Asha does and why she does it.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Museum Model.

passage.text: Asha lifted the delicate model boat with both hands.
She moved it gently because its thin sails could tear.
Then she placed it inside a glass case.
Her class wrote labels for the display.

task.question: What does delicate mean in this passage?

choices.text: Easy to damage
Very noisy
Ready to race

evidenceOptions.text: Asha lifted the delicate model boat with both hands.
She moved it gently because its thin sails could tear.
Then she placed it inside a glass case.

task.explanation: Thin sails that could tear show the boat was easy to damage.

correctFeedback.title: Context clue unlocked
correctFeedback.message: You used the nearby description instead of guessing from the word alone.

lessons.title: Choose proof from the text
lessons.explanation: Text evidence is an exact detail that supports your answer. Pick the sentence that proves your idea best.

workedExample.title: Match claim to proof
workedExample.notice: The claim says the team was ready before the race.
workedExample.think: A sentence about checking equipment proves readiness.
workedExample.prove: It tells exactly what they did before starting.
workedExample.answer: Sentence s2 is the strongest proof.

activities.prompt: Rebuild the scene by choosing the sentence that proves the claim.
activities.hint: Choose proof, not just a related detail.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Canoe Team.

passage.text: The canoe team arrived before sunrise.
They checked each paddle and tightened every life jacket.
A coach blew a whistle near the dock.
The race began after the water became calm.

task.question: Which sentence best supports the claim that the team prepared carefully?

choices.text: Sentence s1
Sentence s2
Sentence s4

evidenceOptions.text: The canoe team arrived before sunrise.
They checked each paddle and tightened every life jacket.
The race began after the water became calm.

task.explanation: Checking paddles and life jackets is direct evidence of careful preparation.

correctFeedback.title: Proof selected
correctFeedback.message: You chose the detail that directly supports the claim.

lessons.title: Understand motives and choices
lessons.explanation: A character's motive is why they act. Connect what a character knows, feels, and does.

workedExample.title: Connect feeling to decision
workedExample.notice: Nia remembers how worried she felt when she lost her key.
workedExample.think: That memory helps explain why she stays to help.
workedExample.prove: Her decision comes right after that memory.
workedExample.answer: Nia stays because she understands the child's worry.

activities.prompt: Connect the character's memory to her decision.
activities.hint: Look for a feeling that explains the action.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Lost Key.

passage.text: Nia remembered the worry she felt when she once lost her own key.
When a younger child searched the playground, Nia stayed to help.
Together they looked beneath the slide and beside the bench.
The child found the key in a jacket pocket.

task.question: Why did Nia decide to help?

choices.text: She understood how worrying it feels to lose a key.
She wanted to miss her bus.
She needed a new jacket.

evidenceOptions.text: Nia remembered the worry she felt when she once lost her own key.
When a younger child searched the playground, Nia stayed to help.
The child found the key in a jacket pocket.

task.explanation: Nia's memory of worry explains why she chose to stay and help.

correctFeedback.title: Motive connected
correctFeedback.message: You linked the character's feeling to her decision.

lessons.title: Put events in order and sum up
lessons.explanation: Sequencing puts events in the order they happened. A summary tells the important events without every small detail.

workedExample.title: Find the order words
workedExample.notice: First, next, and finally tell the order.
workedExample.think: A good summary keeps the important steps.
workedExample.prove: The last sentence gives the result.
workedExample.answer: The class planned, planted, and then watered the garden.

activities.hint: Use the order words in the passage.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Class Garden.

passage.text: First, the class chose a sunny patch beside the school.
Next, they loosened the soil and planted bean seeds.
After that, students made a watering schedule.
By Friday, small green shoots appeared.

task.question: Which order is correct?

choices.text: Watering schedule, shoots, planting
Sunny patch, planting, watering schedule
Planting, sunny patch, shoots

evidenceOptions.text: First, the class chose a sunny patch beside the school.
Next, they loosened the soil and planted bean seeds.
After that, students made a watering schedule.

task.explanation: The order words first, next, and after that give the sequence.

correctFeedback.title: Timeline repaired
correctFeedback.message: You followed the passage's order clues.

activities.prompt: Choose the concise summary that keeps the important events.
activities.hint: Leave out small details that do not change the result.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Class Garden.

passage.text: First, the class chose a sunny patch beside the school.
Next, they loosened the soil and planted bean seeds.
After that, students made a watering schedule.
By Friday, small green shoots appeared.

task.question: Which is the best summary?

choices.text: A class started a garden and cared for it until shoots appeared.
The soil was brown, and Friday came after Thursday.
Students named every bean seed before recess.

evidenceOptions.text: First, the class chose a sunny patch beside the school.
Next, they loosened the soil and planted bean seeds.
By Friday, small green shoots appeared.

task.explanation: This choice includes the important beginning, action, and result without extra details.

correctFeedback.title: Summary shaped
correctFeedback.message: You kept the key events and left out unneeded details.

lessons.title: Notice purpose and point of view
lessons.explanation: Author purpose is why a writer made a text. Point of view is the position or voice through which information is shared.

workedExample.title: Notice the writer's goal
workedExample.notice: The passage gives facts and a safety suggestion.
workedExample.think: Those details help a reader learn how to protect pollinators.
workedExample.prove: It does not tell an invented story or try to sell something.
workedExample.answer: The purpose is to inform and encourage a helpful action.

activities.prompt: Choose the purpose that advances the pollinator quest.
activities.hint: Ask what the writer wants the reader to know or do.

source.attribution: Original LitLearn companion passage: Pollinator Patch.

passage.text: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, helping many plants grow.
A small patch of native flowers can give bees food during the season.
Gardeners can avoid spraying chemicals when bees are visiting.
One bee landed on a purple aster near the path.

task.question: What is the author's main purpose?

choices.text: To inform readers about helping bees
To tell a funny story about a bee
To convince readers to buy purple flowers

evidenceOptions.text: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, helping many plants grow.
A small patch of native flowers can give bees food during the season.
Gardeners can avoid spraying chemicals when bees are visiting.

task.explanation: The passage provides information and a practical action readers can take to help bees.

correctFeedback.title: Purpose spotted
correctFeedback.message: You identified the writer's informative, helpful goal.
